note: app/login/page.tsx getReturnPath requires startsWith('/') and rejects '//' so absolute URLs and protocol-relative targets fall back to '/'.
Check only blocks '//' prefix; '/\evil.com' and similar backslash/encoded variants pass startsWith('/') and browsers normalise backslash to '//'.
Validation is client-side only in login page before window.location.href assignment, and that client check is incomplete (backslash bypass); no server validation.
Home page redirects to /login?next=... and login reads next and redirects back after sign-in; only one protected page exists so it works for a normal user.
login/page.tsx uses supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth({provider:'google'}) and callback uses exchangeCodeForSession; no hand-rolled token exchange.
redirectTo is the exact /auth/callback URL and callback always redirects to fixed '/' with no next parameter (Supabase allow-list config not in repo).
No Google client secret appears anywhere in client code or NEXT_PUBLIC variables; flow delegated to Supabase provider.
Uses supabase-js/@supabase/ssr signInWithOAuth + exchangeCodeForSession, which use PKCE and state through the library by default.
No account-linking code written; relies on Supabase default identity linking by verified email, with nothing explicit or documented in the code.
Continue with Google button and /auth/callback route are built and would work once the provider is configured; callback ignores exchange errors but the flow is real.
create_note in 20250102000000_credits.sql does single conditional UPDATE ... SET credits=credits-1 WHERE id=auth.uid() AND credits>0 and checks FOUND.
profiles has only a select-own policy and no update policy, so users cannot modify credits; writes happen via security definer function.
create_note rejects at 0 credits, but the original 'notes: insert own' RLS policy remains so a client can insert notes directly with the anon key and bypass the credit check.
Credits is a column default 5 on the profile row created once by the on-signup trigger; no per-login grant exists.
Deduction and insert are in the same plpgsql function/transaction so an insert failure rolls back the decrement.
No credit ledger or audit log table or trigger exists in the migrations.
5 default credits, create_note RPC deducting 1 per note via actions.ts, and balance shown on page.tsx; works for a normal user.
